q: While your hands work a skills station, what do you do with your mouth?
a: say the step while your hands do it
say each step as you do it
talk the step while hands work
say it while you do it
why: Say the step while your hands do it. Your mouth and hands stay on the same line.

q: What must you name on medical assessment or you fail?
a: the field impression
field impression / the problem
name the field impression
say the field impression
why: Medical assessment fails if you never name the problem. You must say the field impression.

q: If you finish medical and have no idea what is wrong, what happened?
a: you skipped a check / a box
skipped a check
you skipped a box
lost = skipped a check
why: If you are lost, you skipped a check. If you finish medical with no idea, you skipped a box — look at your notes.

q: What flow do you run on an NRB?
a: 10–15 L/min
10 to 15 L/min
10-15 L/min
NRB 10–15 L/min
why: NRB is 10–15 L/min. Less than 10 is a straw — you suffocate them.

q: What is the adult BVM rate, squeeze time, and when do you stop the squeeze?
a: 1 breath every 6 seconds; squeeze 1 second; until chest rises
1/6s; squeeze ~1s; stop when chest rises
one every 6 seconds; 1-second squeeze; chest rise
1 breath/6s; squeeze 1s; just until chest rises
why: BVM: 1 breath every 6 seconds. Squeeze 1 second. Just until the chest rises.

q: What is the time limit for suction and for the pulse + breathing check?
a: ≤10 seconds each
no more than 10 seconds each
suction ≤10s; pulse+breathing ≤10s
10 seconds max for both
why: Suction no more than 10 seconds. Pulse + breathing check no more than 10 seconds.

q: What is Chapter 10 in book form for these skills?
a: the skill sheet
Chapter 10 = the skill sheet in book form
skill sheet in book form
the skill sheet (book form)
why: Review Chapter 10. That chapter is the skill sheet in book form.

q: After you gather tank, regulator, mask, and wrench, what is cracking the tank?
a: quick open then close to blow dirt out of the outlet
quick open, then close; blows dirt out
brief open/close to clear the outlet
crack = quick open then close (dirt out)
why: Crack the tank. Quick open, then close. Blows dirt out of the outlet. Open = lefty-loosey.

q: How do you seat the regulator so it is right?
a: two pins in two holes first, then screw down; sits at a right angle
pins first, then screw; right angle (tilted = not seated)
pins in holes first; screw down; right angle
two pins first; screw; right angle — tilted means not seated
why: Seat the regulator. Two pins go in the two holes first. Then screw it down. It should sit at a right angle. Tilted = not seated.

q: After opening the tank one full turn, what gauge reading is about full, and what do you listen for?
a: about 2000 PSI; listen for a hiss / leak
~2000 PSI; hiss (leak often dead brass washer)
full ~2000 PSI; listen for hiss
about 2000 PSI; hiss = leak check
why: Check the gauge. Full tank is about 2000 PSI. Listen for a hiss. A leak is usually a dead brass washer.

q: What flow do you set from the start on the tank build, and why not start low?
a: 10–15 L/min from the start; do not start low and forget
set 10–15 first; do not start low and forget
10–15 from the start so you do not forget
turn flow to 10–15 L/min from the start
why: Turn flow to 10–15 L/min from the start. Do not start low and forget. Shortcut: set 10–15 first so “adjust to at least 10” is already done.

q: Is 0.5 L/min a treatment on an NRB?
a: no — not a treatment
no; 0.5 L/min is not a treatment
no — NRB below 10 restricts breathing
no
why: 0.5 L/min is not a treatment. NRB below 10 restricts breathing.

q: If you are not holding the O2 tank, what do you do with it, and why?
a: lay it down; standing tank with snapped neck becomes a missile
lay it down — snapped neck = missile
lay the tank down; standing + snapped neck = missile
lay it down so it cannot become a missile
why: If you are not holding the tank, lay it down. A standing tank with a snapped neck becomes a missile.

q: On the BVM station the patient is unresponsive, not breathing, with a weak pulse of 60. What does that mean for you?
a: alive, not breathing — keep going
alive not breathing; keep going with airway/BVM
weak pulse 60 = alive, not breathing; keep going
keep going — alive but not breathing
why: The station says: unresponsive, not breathing, weak pulse of 60. Alive, not breathing. Keep going.

q: How do you run suction after you find a mouth full of vomit?
a: on+test; measure mouth-corner to earlobe; insert OFF; ON coming out circling ≤10s
test suction; measure; insert OFF; suction ON on the way out; circle; ≤10s
measure corner to earlobe; insert OFF; ON while out; ≤10 seconds
turn on/test; measure; insert OFF; suction ON coming out; ≤10s
why: Turn it on. Test that it sucks. Measure corner of mouth to earlobe. Insert with suction OFF. Suction ON while you come out. Circle. No more than 10 seconds.

q: How do you measure and insert an OPA?
a: corner of mouth to earlobe; insert sideways; twist 90°
measure mouth-corner to earlobe; sideways then twist 90°
corner-to-earlobe; insert sideways; twist 90 degrees
OPA: measure corner to earlobe; sideways; twist 90°
why: OPA. Measure corner of mouth to earlobe. Insert sideways. Twist 90°. The station says: no gag — patient accepts it.

q: On BVM, what oxygen setup and grip do you use once the airway is held open?
a: high-flow O2 at 15 L/min; C-E grip; seal the mask
BVM on 15 L/min; C-E grip; seal
15 L/min high-flow; C-E grip; seal the mask
high-flow 15 L/min with C-E grip seal
why: BVM on high-flow oxygen at 15 L/min. C-E grip. Seal the mask.

q: The printed sheet wants room air first, then oxygen after ventilations work. Class put 15 L on right away. What do you do on test day?
a: do whatever that day’s sheet says
follow that day’s sheet
do the printed sheet order for that day
that day’s sheet wins
why: The printed sheet may have you bag on room air first, then add oxygen after ventilations are working. Do whatever that day’s sheet says. In class he put 15 L on right away.
